title: Signals Notebook vs Labguru: Which ELN Platform Fits Your Lab?
summary: Compare Signals Notebook vs Labguru across ELN, LIMS, inventory, integrations, compliance, pricing, and scalability to choose the right platform for your lab.
body_markdown:
## **TL;DR**


- Signals Notebook from Revvity Signals is a cloud-native ELN focused on scientific documentation, chemistry workflows, collaboration, instrument data, inventory, and enterprise R&D.
- Labguru combines ELN, LIMS, inventory, equipment management, workflow automation, and laboratory informatics in one platform.
- Signals Notebook stands out for native ChemDraw integration and chemistry-centered R&D, while Labguru places more emphasis on connecting experiments with samples, inventory, equipment, and laboratory operations.
- The right choice depends on scientific discipline, LIMS requirements, inventory complexity, integrations, compliance needs, pricing, and long-term data architecture.


When comparing **Signals Notebook vs Labguru** , laboratories are looking at two cloud-based scientific platforms that both replace paper notebooks but extend in different directions.


Signals Notebook focuses on enterprise scientific documentation, chemistry, multidisciplinary research, and analytical data workflows. Labguru combines notebook functionality with LIMS, inventory, equipment, sample tracking, and broader laboratory operations.

## **Signals Notebook vs Labguru at a Glance**


### **What Is Signals Notebook?**


Signals Notebook is Revvity Signals' cloud-native electronic lab notebook for pharmaceutical, biotechnology, chemical, materials, formulation, and other research organizations.


Its current capabilities include:


- Experiment capture and collaboration
- Native ChemDraw integration
- Chemical search and stoichiometry
- Inventory and material management
- Signals DLX instrument connectivity
- Open APIs for LIMS and enterprise systems
- Electronic signatures and audit trails
- Integration with the broader Signals analytics ecosystem


Revvity currently lists Signals Notebook Standard at **$1,425 per user annually** . Enterprise configurations may involve different requirements and commercial terms.


### **What Is Labguru?**


[Labguru](https://www.scispot.com/blog/labguru-review) is a laboratory informatics platform combining ELN, LIMS, inventory, equipment management, and workflow automation.


Labguru connects experiments with samples, reagents, storage locations, equipment, protocols, and laboratory processes. Its LIMS also supports reporting, instrument management, workflow automation, electronic approvals, and large research datasets.

## **Signals Notebook vs Labguru Feature Comparison**


### **ELN and Scientific Documentation**


Signals Notebook is centered on experimental documentation and scientific collaboration. Native ChemDraw integration supports chemical structures, reactions, stoichiometry calculations, and chemical search directly within notebook workflows.


Labguru's ELN connects experiments with its LIMS, inventory, equipment, and request-management capabilities. This makes laboratory records part of a broader operational environment rather than a standalone notebook.


Labs evaluating additional ELN options can also review Scispot's[Benchling vs Signals Notebook comparison](https://www.scispot.com/blog/benchling-vs-signals-notebook) .


### **LIMS, Samples, and Inventory**


This is one of the clearest differences.


Labguru provides native LIMS capabilities alongside ELN functionality. Its platform supports sample tracking, storage locations, quantities, expiration dates, workflow automation, reporting, equipment scheduling, and inventory records connected directly with experiments.


Signals Notebook provides integrated inventory and materials management, including barcode workflows and chemical inventory, but its primary product category remains ELN rather than LIMS. It can connect to external LIMS platforms through APIs.

### **Instrument Connectivity and Integrations**


Signals Notebook connects analytical instruments through Signals DLX and supports REST APIs for integrating LIMS, ERP, and other enterprise applications.


Labguru supports instrument management and orchestration alongside broader laboratory automation. Its workflow tools can automate processes spanning data capture, analysis, and laboratory operations.

### **Compliance and Data Integrity**


Signals Notebook provides SOC 2 Type II controls, audit trails, electronic signatures, role-based access controls, validation documentation, and functionality designed to support 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.


Labguru supports audit trails, electronic signatures, version history, access controls, and 21 CFR Part 11-oriented workflows. Labguru also completed a SOC 2 Type 2 examination in 2024.


Regulated laboratories should validate their exact configuration, SOPs, validation responsibilities, and intended use rather than assuming software certification alone establishes compliance.


## **Which Labs Should Consider Each Platform?**


### **Chemistry and Pharmaceutical R&D Teams**


Signals Notebook is particularly relevant for medicinal chemistry, synthetic chemistry, formulation, materials science, and multidisciplinary pharmaceutical research where ChemDraw and chemistry-aware workflows are central.


### **Biotech, CRO, and Operational Research Labs**


Labguru may appeal to organizations that want experiments, samples, inventory, equipment, LIMS workflows, and laboratory operations managed within one environment.


For additional context, see Scispot's[Benchling vs Labguru comparison](https://www.scispot.com/blog/benchling-vs-labguru) .


### **Labs Comparing Total Cost**


Signals Notebook Standard currently publishes a $1,425 per-user annual list price. Buyers evaluating either platform should also account for implementation, validation, integrations, data migration, training, additional modules, and ongoing administration.

## **What to Consider Before Choosing**


### **ELN-First vs Integrated Lab Operations**


The central decision is architectural.


Signals Notebook is primarily an ELN that can expand through inventory, Signals DLX, APIs, analytics, and the broader Revvity Signals ecosystem.


Labguru packages ELN, LIMS, inventory, equipment, and laboratory informatics more directly within one application.


### **Connected Data and AI Readiness**


Modern labs increasingly need experimental records, sample metadata, instrument outputs, reports, and operational data to remain connected and searchable.
